description: This statement has three errors. Claim 1 prints the same eye exam twice on one date, charging the $40 copay twice; claim 2's annual wellness visit charges the $20 office-visit copay although preventive services cost the member nothing; and claim 3's member-share total is $15.00 higher than its only line, an X-ray of the chest. A careful reviewer should flag all three: a duplicate line, a preventive cost-sharing charge and a claim total that does not add up.

sources.what: An exact duplicate matches another claim line on beneficiary, provider, date of service, procedure code and billed amount
sources.source: CMS, Medicare Claims Processing Manual (Pub. 100-04), ch. 1, §120.2 Exact Duplicates, https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/guidance/manuals/downloads/clm104c01.pdf

sources.what: MA organizations may not charge deductibles, copayments or coinsurance for in-network Medicare-covered preventive services (paragraph (k))
The preventive services this rule covers include the annual wellness visit (paragraph (l))
sources.source: Cornell LII, 42 CFR 410.152 Amounts of payment, https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/410.152

sources.what: The EOB must report billed, approved, plan-paid and member amounts per item and as cumulative totals, so a claim's printed totals must add up its lines
sources.source: eCFR, 42 CFR 422.111(k)(1) and (k)(2), Disclosure requirements (Part C explanation of benefits: amounts per item and year-to-date totals), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-C/section-422.111
